pr.title: Lead projector.bot with the agent loop, and follow field's recording project as the example
pr.head: 3750f613eda8ebb75236765bc4dba3572616514c

summary: projector.bot is Projector's marketing site, a static Next.js page that lives in web/ and builds every route at build time. Until this change it introduced Projector as project plans kept in Git. It said nothing about the parts people now meet first: the panel above the Claude Code prompt, its inbox of agent questions, requests, and notices, and the pull request summaries.

This pull request rewrites the front page around the agent loop. A new hero carries a working copy of Projector's panel that a visitor can click through. New sections follow for the inbox, the summaries, the spec, build, review, and fix loop, sessions left working, and smaller tools. The plans-in-Git explanation stays as the section under the loop, and the worked example moves from trip's session switcher to the recording project in the public audiofield/field repository.
Nothing outside web/ changes, and nothing on the page talks to a server. The demo panel keeps all of its state in React and resets with a button.

cards.title: Review history so far
cards.html:
• First review, at 0d2bc8a: one finding and two suggestions. The finding was that the inbox section said a ready pull request "waits for its first review", although the panel also shows ready after a push takes clean off a reviewed pull request. One suggestion was that two lines of the demo panel ended one column away from the ages' column. The other was that the digit keys did nothing in a pull request's drawer.
  • Second review, at 3750f61: clean. The ready entry now says the pull request waits for a review of its current head, and the author took both suggestions.

The site lints, type-checks, and builds, and the field example's commits, reviews, and numbers match GitHub.

groups.title: The hero and its working panel
groups.kicker: A clickable copy of Projector's panel, drawn in its dark theme
intro: The hero now leads with the headline "Agents plan, build, and review. You make the calls." and puts the install command under it. Below sits InboxDemo, a client component that draws the panel as monospaced text: four of your pull requests, one review request, then the inbox items newest first.

Each line is a button. A pull request opens a drawer with its role, branch, size, checks, labels, and findings by file. An item opens a drawer with its detail, its options, and the actions I don't understand, Discuss, Dismiss, and Snooze. An option or Discuss fills the fake prompt box under the panel, the way the real panel fills Claude Code's prompt. The iPhone request's Start moves it to starting and, after a timer, to ready.

files.note: All the demo's data and behavior. Line widths are counted by hand against WIDTH = 92 so that the ages line up.

checks.text: prActions lists a pull request drawer's actions once, and two things use that list: the drawer's buttons and the keyboard handler below. So 7 and 8, and 8 and 9 while a dismissal waits for you to confirm it, work by key as well as by click.
The handler acts only while a drawer is open: an item's, where 0 also closes it, or a pull request's. It ignores keys pressed with a modifier.
The review counted the columns. 0: is six characters, so an open item's top line ends at column 92. That is the ages' column, where the list's rows, the header (line 859), and the key hint also end.

files.note: Headline, install command, description, and the "Try the panel" guide beside the demo.
